estimatedRowsHint: Estimated from PostgreSQL's table statistics: the activity counters were reset (pg_stat_reset, a crash or a restore) and the table hasn't been vacuumed or analyzed since. The dead count only covers changes since the reset. Run ANALYZE on the table for exact numbers.

table.label: Table
table.help: Table name — grouped by schema below.

rows.label: Rows (live/dead)
rows.help: Estimated live row count and dead (deleted or updated but not yet reclaimed by VACUUM) row count for this table, from pg_stat_user_tables.

deadPct.label: Dead %
deadPct.help: Percent of this table's rows that are dead (deleted or updated but not yet reclaimed by VACUUM). High values mean autovacuum is falling behind.

lastVacuum.label: Last vacuum
lastVacuum.help: When this table was last vacuumed (manual or automatic), reclaiming dead row space.

lastAnalyze.label: Last analyze
lastAnalyze.help: When this table's query-planner statistics were last refreshed (manual or automatic).

wraparound.label: Wraparound age
wraparound.help: How many transactions old this table's oldest row is. Approaching the ~2 billion limit risks transaction ID wraparound — keep autovacuum running.

cacheHit.label: Cache hit %
cacheHit.help: Percent of this table's reads served from memory rather than disk (target: above 95%). A single hot table can run low even when the database-wide average on the Dashboard looks healthy.

size.label: Size
size.help: Total on-disk size, including all of this table's indexes. Refreshed on the background table-metrics cycle (every 5 minutes by default), not computed live on every load — kept off the hot path since it's expensive to compute for every table on a large database.

deepScan.autoTitle: Also runs automatically every night — see Settings.
deepScan.runTitle: Runs every table's advisor checks now, across the whole database, and records the results — the same thing that runs nightly (see Settings).

allSchemasHidden: All schemas are hidden — use the Schemas button above to show some.

analyze.label: Analyze all
analyze.confirm_one: Runs ANALYZE on {{count}} table, one after another, so their row counts and planner statistics are fresh. ANALYZE reads a sample of each table; reads and writes carry on while it runs.
analyze.confirm_other: Runs ANALYZE on {{count}} tables, one after another, so their row counts and planner statistics are fresh. ANALYZE reads a sample of each table; reads and writes carry on while it runs.
analyze.skipped_one: {{count}} skipped: DbButler's role may not analyze it (needs table ownership, or pg_maintain on PostgreSQL 17+).
analyze.skipped_other: {{count}} skipped: DbButler's role may not analyze them (needs table ownership, or pg_maintain on PostgreSQL 17+).

vacuum.label: Vacuum all
vacuum.confirm_one: Runs VACUUM (ANALYZE) on {{count}} table, one after another: dead rows become reusable space and the statistics are refreshed. Reads and writes carry on, but VACUUM reads every table and writes its changes, so on a busy server prefer a quiet moment. This is not VACUUM FULL — nothing is locked against use, and files don't shrink.
vacuum.confirm_other: Runs VACUUM (ANALYZE) on {{count}} tables, one after another: dead rows become reusable space and the statistics are refreshed. Reads and writes carry on, but VACUUM reads every table and writes its changes, so on a busy server prefer a quiet moment. This is not VACUUM FULL — nothing is locked against use, and files don't shrink.
vacuum.skipped_one: {{count}} skipped: DbButler's role may not vacuum it (needs table ownership, or pg_maintain on PostgreSQL 17+).
vacuum.skipped_other: {{count}} skipped: DbButler's role may not vacuum them (needs table ownership, or pg_maintain on PostgreSQL 17+).

row.deadTuplesUnchanged: Dead tuples unchanged ({{dead}}) — VACUUM completed without error, but something else may be holding the rows back from actually being reclaimed: check Activity for a long-running or idle-in-transaction session, or Advisor → Replication Advisor for an inactive replication slot.
row.statsRefreshed: Query planner statistics refreshed for this table.

analyze.title: Refresh the query planner's statistics for this table. Fast, no meaningful lock — safe to run any time, e.g. after a bulk load.
analyze.confirmMessage: Refreshes the query planner's statistics for this table. Fast, no meaningful lock — safe to run any time.
analyze.label: Analyze

vacuum.title: Reclaim dead-row space and refresh statistics (VACUUM ANALYZE). Runs alongside normal reads/writes, but uses real I/O — avoid running on many large tables at once.
vacuum.confirmMessage: Runs VACUUM ANALYZE: reclaims dead-row space and refreshes statistics. Runs alongside normal reads/writes, but uses real I/O — avoid running on many large tables at once.
vacuum.label: Vacuum

resetStats.title: Reset this table's cumulative counters (dead/live tuple counts, index scan counts) back to zero. Useful right after a manual Vacuum to see a clean baseline. Does not change any data.
resetStats.confirmMessage: Resets this table's cumulative counters (dead/live tuple counts, index scan counts) to zero. Does not change any data.
resetStats.label: Reset stats

avgWidth.label: Avg width
avgWidth.hint: Average on-disk size of this column's values, in bytes. Shows — until the table has been analyzed at least once.

nullPct.label: Null %
nullPct.hint: Share of this table's rows where this column is NULL.

distinct.label: Distinct
distinct.hint: Estimated number of distinct values (pg_stats.n_distinct). A non-negative number is an absolute count; a negative number is a fraction of all rows (e.g. -0.5 means about half the rows are distinct).

statsTarget.label: Stats target
statsTarget.hint: How many rows Postgres samples to build this column's planner statistics. "default" uses the server-wide default_statistics_target (100 unless changed) rather than a per-column override.

indexed.label: Indexed
indexed.hint: Whether this column is part of any index (alone or combined with others).

storage.label: Storage
storage.hint: How large values in this column can be stored: plain (always inline, never TOASTed), extended/main (may move out-of-line into TOAST, compressed), external (moves out-of-line uncompressed).

storage.title: Storage
storage.heapHint: This table's own data pages — everything except TOAST and indexes.
storage.toastHint: Large text/bytea/jsonb values stored out-of-line, compressed, from the main table.
storage.indexesHint: Combined size of every index on this table. Derived (total minus heap minus TOAST), not its own separate measurement.
storage.totalHint: Everything for this table combined — heap + TOAST + indexes.

autovacuum.title: Autovacuum & updates
autovacuum.autovacuumHint: Whether autovacuum runs on this table at all — should almost always be Enabled.
autovacuum.vacuumScaleFactorHint: Fraction of a table's rows that must be dead before autovacuum runs. A table-level override, when set, replaces the server-wide default shown here.
autovacuum.analyzeScaleFactorHint: Fraction of a table's rows that must change before autovacuum re-analyzes it (refreshes planner statistics).
autovacuum.fillfactorHint: Percent of each page Postgres fills before starting a new one — the rest is headroom for HOT updates.
autovacuum.hotRatioHint: Share of updates that avoided touching any index (Heap-Only Tuple). Low means most updates are paying full index-maintenance cost.
autovacuum.vacuumStatusHint: Whether a VACUUM (manual or autovacuum) is actively running on this table right now, from pg_stat_progress_vacuum. Only reflects the current instant, not history.
